project_tracker_diagnostic: Hispid biennial/short-lived perennial with yellow rays surrounding a dark brown-purple hemispheric to ovoid disk; leaves and stems conspicuously rough-hairy.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — natural Purola flora lists R. hirta; Travis — UT herbarium index documents R. hirta; Williamson — dedicated county treatment documents R. hirta and notes var. pulcherrima if accepted.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Species-level canonical entry; accepted variety pulcherrima taught internally.

morphology_keys.life_cycle: Biennial or short-lived perennial, sometimes flowering first year.
morphology_keys.leaves: Variable; basal lanceolate to elliptic, stem leaves linear to ovate-lanceolate; rough-hairy.
morphology_keys.heads: Yellow rays around a dark purplish-brown hemispheric/ovoid disk.

photo_strategy.method: LEARNER FAST-FILL — exact-species licensed iNaturalist/Commons set
photo_strategy.selection_logic: Keep only exact Rudbeckia hirta / accepted local var. pulcherrima material with licenses that permit private/noncommercial study. Remove prior all-rights-reserved gallery rows.
photo_strategy.visual_priority: flower-head architecture + flowering habit + rough/hairy vegetative texture
photo_strategy.remaining_polish: Replace/add a tighter labeled trichome/leaf macro later if a clearly diagnostic licensed image is found.

taxonomic_note: Current Kew accepts Rudbeckia hirta with four varieties, including var. pulcherrima. Williamson County treats local plants as R. hirta (var. pulcherrima if accepted); the project keeps the stable species-level canonical entry and teaches var. pulcherrima as the likely/local infraspecific concept rather than creating a duplicate species.
look_here_first: Start with texture: black-eyed Susan is conspicuously rough-hairy on stems and leaves. Then confirm yellow rays around a dark brown-purple raised disk. Unlike R. amplexicaulis, its leaves do not clasp the stem.

infraspecific_lesson.Rudbeckia hirta var. pulcherrima: Accepted by current Kew and explicitly noted as the likely/local variety in the Williamson County treatment; taught within the species-level learner.

comparisons.key_distinctions: R. hirta = rough/hispid non-clasping leaves; R. amplexicaulis = smoother clasping leaves; R. maxima = giant East Texas perennial with enormous glaucous basal leaves.
